statement: Resolved 2026-08-25. The object is Rumsey 12186.101, 'Terre Artiche', in Atlante Veneto Tomo I; the plate has been examined at full IIIF resolution.
why_it_matters: Act III's central object is no longer unseen. What the plate depicts may now be stated from the plate.
next_action: None. Superseded by ant-gap-atlante-epitome-attribution for the remaining question of which publication the sequence belongs to.

statement: Resolved 2026-08-25 for Atlante Veneto Tomo I. The polar section runs Rumsey 12186.100 to .107: six text leaves headed for both poles, two engraved plates ('Terre Artiche' 12186.101 and 'Polo Artiche' 12186.104), both classified Arctic, and the section then closes into Idrografia at .108. No southern polar plate was cut for this sequence.
why_it_matters: The Act III finding inverts, and improves, as anticipated: the south is what Coronelli does not attend to, and the asymmetry now rests on the structure of the catalogued sequence rather than on absence of search results.
next_action: None for Tomo I. Whether any southern polar plate exists elsewhere in the thirteen-volume Atlante Veneto is tracked separately as ant-gap-atlante-plates.

statement: Milanesi's Coronelli monograph has not been consulted, and the Terre Artiche plate now carries a specific patron whose bearing on the plate is unknown.
why_it_matters: The plate is dedicated to Conte Ercole Pepoli. Without Milanesi, Act III would read a dedicated commercial plate as if it were Coronelli's personal cosmology, which is the exact error the claim ledger flags as high risk.
next_action: Closed by declaration: Milanesi's monograph is not consulted, and ant-clm-coronelli-belief is held permanently at medium confidence for that reason rather than pending its arrival. What the claim rests on is Coronelli's own voice at Atlante Veneto printed pp. 70 and 76 and Epitome p. 266, which is enough to say he distinguished inherited from reported material. What it does not rest on is any account of the Frari workshop's commissioning practice, and no such account is available to this project. The Terre Artiche plate's dedication to Conte Ercole Pepoli is recorded on ant-obj-coronelli-terre-artiche as a fact of the sheet with its bearing unread, and Act III makes no claim that the plate expresses Coronelli's personal cosmology - a dedicated commercial plate is not evidence of private belief, and the distinction the claim does make survives without it. #163 established that the volume can be described from its publisher's record but not cited from it, and that remains the position. Acquiring the Brepols volume would upgrade this claim to high, not unblock it.

statement: No plate showing the southern polar region has been identified anywhere in the Atlante Veneto. Four candidate plates have been proposed but not verified.
why_it_matters: The object register held a placeholder that had to resolve or be deleted, and the working assumption behind it - that Tomo I carries no southern polar plate - was wrong.
next_action: Closed: the plate exists, and this row's premise was mistaken. Atlante Veneto Tomo I carries Polo Antarctico at plate 12186.050 (Rumsey), a 37 x 37 cm south polar atlas sheet examined at full resolution on 2026-09-08 and now filed as ant-obj-coronelli-atlante-polar, which was the placeholder this row existed to resolve. It draws no land at all - meridians converging on a marked pole, a scale to 85 degrees, labelled latitude circles, and a Magellan cartouche that rejects two claims of prior knowledge. The other three candidates are settled as well, two of them negatively. Planisfero Meridionale (12186.040) is a celestial map, the southern sky rather than the southern earth: examined, and it carries the Magellanic cloud, Dorado, Crux and Argo Navis around the south celestial pole. No plate called Costellazioni Celesti del Polo Antartico exists in the Rumsey catalogue under that name, and the Planisfero is most likely what the candidate was reaching for. America Meridionale (12186.097) is confirmed and is a South America sheet. The Libro dei Globi line is a dead end here: Rumsey's set (publication 10714) is described in its own title as counterproof plates for a celestial globe, and its south polar calotte (10714.077, .078) is celestial; the terrestrial south polar calotte is 10070.026, already examined in #162. One limit stands and is not closed by this: Rumsey holds only Tomo I of the Atlante Veneto's thirteen folios, so "the remaining volumes" have not been audited and cannot be from here. What is now established is that the volume this project can reach gives the south pole a plate of its own and leaves it empty.

statement: Both verified Greenwich objects state no reuse licence; the 1910 ice chart carries a Crown copyright credit line.
why_it_matters: The two objects the essay most wants to reproduce are the two whose terms are unknown. Both are research_only until RMG Images answers in writing.
next_action: Closed by declaration: no Royal Museums Greenwich object is reproduced in this essay, and none will be until RMG Images answers in writing. Four verified objects are affected, not the two this row was written for - ant-obj-cook-southern-hemisphere-1777 (PAI4123), its second impression ant-obj-cook-southern-hemisphere-1777-alt (G201:3/3), ant-obj-ukho-ice-chart-1910 (G288:1/2(2), which additionally carries a Crown copyright credit line) and ant-obj-ukho-ice-chart-1874 (NTY288:1/2(1)). All four stay rights_status rights_review_required and reproduction_use research_only, and all four are cited from their catalogue records rather than shown. Acts IV and VII therefore describe their anchor objects in words and link to the Greenwich record instead of carrying an image. This closes the row as a published limit, not as a grant: a reply from RMG Images would reopen it, and could only add reproductions - never remove this statement of what the essay did without.

statement: Greenwich holds at least two records for the 1777 southern-hemisphere chart and they have not been compared.
why_it_matters: The essay must name the copy it reproduces. Two records for one chart is the ambiguity the register exists to close.
next_action: Closed. rmgc-object-543571 is G201:3/3, a second impression of the same plate with a Forster attribution and different measurements. The essay reproduces PAI4123 unless a state comparison says otherwise.

statement: No holding copy or plate state has been identified for the Mercator 1569 world map.
why_it_matters: The southern coastline differs across states. A comparison of 'the Ortelius world map' with no state named compares nothing in particular.
next_action: Narrowed 2026-09-08: two of the three objects are settled and only Mercator remains. Ortelius is Rumsey 10000.011, the Theatrum Orbis Terrarum first edition (Antwerp, Gillis Coppens van Diest, M.D.LXX), plate signed by Frans Hogenberg, southern coast read as TERRA AVSTRALIS NONDVM COGNITA - and it is the same physical copy the Dacia programme already cites, so one volume now serves two programmes. Fine is Rumsey 15894.000, and the copy is the 1540 Christian Wechel issue dated M.D.XL on the plate rather than the 1531 first issue, southern coast read as TERRA AVSTRALIS RECenter inuenta sed nondum plene cognita. Both are verified with the state named, which is what this row asked for. Mercator's 1569 wall map is not in Rumsey and only a handful of copies survive; the object row points at the BnF, which blocks this environment. What remains is to select one holding copy of the Mercator, or to record the decision to argue Act I from a documented facsimile and say so.

statement: No Bellingshausen chart has been located in a named repository.
why_it_matters: The 1820 priority discussion cannot be illustrated from the Russian side, which would leave the essay arguing priority from British and American material alone.
next_action: Closed by declaration: no Bellingshausen chart has been located in a named repository, and Act V's priority discussion is made from British and American material and from Debenham's translation, with that asymmetry stated in the essay rather than left for a reader to notice. This follows ant-gap-bellingshausen-translation, which closed the same way on the same claim. The consequence is recorded on ant-clm-first-sighting: its map_object_ids reference to ant-obj-bellingshausen-atlas was deliberately unresolved pending this row, and is now removed rather than left pointing at an object nobody has seen. What survives is the argument the claim actually makes, which is definitional and needs no plate - the disagreement between Bellingshausen, Bransfield and Palmer is about what counts as a sighting, and that can be set out from the texts. That the Russian side cannot be illustrated is itself a finding about which archives are reachable, and belongs in the essay as one.

statement: The essay's access to Bellingshausen is through Debenham's 1945 English edition.
why_it_matters: Priority claims often turn on the wording of what was seen. A translation is an interpretation and may not silently stand in for the Russian text.
next_action: Closed by declaration: the dependence on Debenham's 1945 translation is now recorded on ant-clm-first-sighting and ant-pri-bellingshausen-1820 rather than left implicit. Consulting the Russian text for the passages the essay quotes remains open future work and would upgrade, not unblock, this claim.

statement: The Wilkes atlas is located at the Library of Congress with a digitised copy, but no individual sheet or charted position has been identified.
why_it_matters: The programme's flagship ghost-geography case is currently a general recollection that Ross sailed over land Wilkes charted. Which land, at what position, on which sheet, is unknown.
next_action: Closed: the plate is No. 70 in the Atlas of the Narrative of the United States Exploring Expedition (ant-obj-wilkes-antarctic-chart, now verified), examined via the American Geographical Society Library’s digitised copy since LoC itself blocks this environment. Termination Land is named on it, drawn as unsurveyed (dotted) coastline, at an approximate position of 94.5-96.7°E, 67.9-70.1°S read from the plate’s own graticule. ant-ghost-wilkes-segment’s source_locator now cites the plate; its geometry stays empty on purpose – a pixel-read position is not a survey-grade georeference. A rigorous georeference, and locating the more easterly named peaks (Ringgold’s Knoll and neighbours), remain open future work.

statement: The Endurance22 site returned 403 and the Antarctic Treaty HSM 93 entry could not be retrieved. The 1915 position now has a reviewed source; the 2022 position still does not.
why_it_matters: The Coda compares a 1915 reported position with a 2022 confirmed one. Neither figure is currently held from a citable source, and secondary reporting conflates the two.
next_action: The 2022 position is now held: Measure 18 (2022/2024), ant-src-hsm-93 (verified), 68°44′21″ S, 52°19′47″ W, 1500m radius. What remains is the 1915 side of the comparison – read Bergman, Mearns and Stuart''s chronometer-error companion paper (Journal of Navigation 75(6), 2022) for the transcribed position and its uncertainty, which ant-gap-worsley-workings has the archive identification for but not yet the position – before ant-clm-wreck-distance can be drawn.

statement: Worsley's navigational records have not been located in a named archive, but Bergman and Stuart transcribed his logbook and replicated its calculations in print.
why_it_matters: Without them the dataset cannot distinguish an observed fix from a dead-reckoned position, which is the whole subject of Act VIII.
next_action: Closed: read in full (ant-src-bergman-stuart-weddell-navigation). The workbooks are Canterbury Museum 2001.177.1 (1 Aug 1914 - 30 Aug 1915, covers the besetment) and 2001.177.20 (30 Aug 1915 - 13 May 1916, covers the sinking and boat journey) – both at Canterbury Museum, not Scott Polar Research Institute as an earlier, unverified note had it. Dated positions transcribed: 27 October 1915 abandonment, "Landed on Floe 69°5′ S 51°32′ W"; 21 November 1915 sinking, 68°39′30″ S 52°26′30″ W. No coordinate is given for the moment of besetment itself (19 January 1915, see ant-gap-besetment-date) – the log simply reads "Fast in pack", repeated daily. ant-clm-fix-vs-interpolation can now be checked against real dated entries rather than waiting on the archive.

statement: No reviewed table of dated Endurance positions has been compiled from a primary or scholarly source.
why_it_matters: A drift track drawn from a narrative is an illustration. The interactive claims to show recorded positions and must be able to cite each one.
next_action: Compile positions from Worsley and Shackleton with page locators, then mark which are observed and which are inferred. The boat journey no longer waits on this: its fourteen noon positions are compiled from ant-src-bergman-caird-navigation with the log's own DR-or-observed label on each. What is left is the drift year, whose dated entries ant-src-bergman-stuart-weddell-navigation transcribes from workbook 2001.177.1 without this project having worked through them.

statement: The Greenwich record dates the ice chart 1910 and 1874, and a separate 1874 record exists; the two sheets have not been compared.
why_it_matters: If the 1910 sheet revises an 1874 compilation, Act VII can show a synthesis being corrected rather than merely accumulating.
next_action: Closed. NTY288:1/2(1) is the 1874 compilation, published 1879, listing Cook through Ross plus Towson's iceberg papers. The 1910 sheet adds Scott 1901-4 and Shackleton 1908-9. The revision is demonstrable from the two titles.

statement: No scholarship has been consulted that attributes any specific southern ghost feature to mirage, refraction or ice.
why_it_matters: Attributing a cause to an error is a much stronger claim than recording that it was later removed, and the specification flags it as high risk.
next_action: Closed: a literature search for peer-reviewed work attributing a named southern ghost feature to mirage, refraction or ice misidentification found nothing citable. ant-clm-mirage-causation is source_checked with that finding recorded rather than left unreviewed; no causal statement is drafted. A specific attribution found later would reopen this rather than be added silently.

statement: Headland's chronology has not been consulted, so no date in this programme has been checked against a reference work.
why_it_matters: Dates are the spine of Acts V to VIII and are the easiest thing to get quietly wrong.
next_action: Closed by declaration: no date in this programme has been checked against a reference chronology, and the essay says so rather than implying a check that did not happen. Every date in observations.csv and expedition-phases.csv comes from the expedition source that reports it or from the holding institution's catalogue record - a citable provenance, but not an independent one: a date transcribed correctly from a source that was itself wrong would pass every gate here. Headland's chronology remains the obvious control, and consulting it would upgrade these dates rather than unblock them, since nothing in Acts V to VIII is withheld for want of it. A disagreement found later between a transcribed date and the chronology reopens this row rather than being corrected silently.

statement: Sources seen during the audit give the besetment of Endurance as both 18 and 19 January 1915.
why_it_matters: The drift dataset is dated throughout, and the first date in it is the one everything else is measured from.
next_action: Closed: Worsley's own log entry (1915: 64, transcribed in ant-src-bergman-stuart-weddell-navigation) reads "Fast in pack" on 19 January 1915, repeated daily until it becomes "F. in P." on 2 February and is eventually dropped. 19 January is the date the drift dataset should use; the 18 January reading is recorded as a disagreement rather than dropped, per this row's own instruction, since it is not what Worsley's log itself says.

statement: No Dumont d'Urville atlas plate has been identified.
why_it_matters: Wilkes, d'Urville and Ross were charting overlapping coast in the same season. With one of the three located, Act V can describe the competition but cannot show it.
next_action: Progress 2026-08-27: a Dumont d''Urville atlas plate is now identified. Gallica blocks this environment, but Heidelberg University Library''s own digitisation (ant-obj-durville-atlas, https://digi.ub.uni-heidelberg.de/diglit/dumont1846atlasbd2) is free and confirmed to hold plates 168-172 of the Atlas pittoresque, T. 2 – the range reported for the Terre Adelie landing sequence. What remains: read each plate''s printed caption to confirm subject and date (not yet transcribed), and locate the Atlas hydrographique, which is not among Heidelberg''s four digitised items and is what Act V actually needs for a coastline position to compare against Wilkes and Ross – the pittoresque plates are illustrated scenes, not charts.

statement: The voyage contributions recorded for the 1874 and 1910 charts come from the catalogue titles, not from reading the sheets.
why_it_matters: A title says which voyages were compiled. It does not say what each contributed, or where on the sheet, which is what the annotated view needs.
next_action: Closed by declaration: the voyage lists on both charts are transcribed from their Greenwich catalogue titles and are cited as titles, not as readings of the sheets. That supports what ant-clm-cumulative-chart actually asserts - that the 1910 chart compiles eleven voyages between 1772 and 1909 - and it supports the revision the two titles demonstrate between them, the 1874 list ending at Ross and Towson's iceberg papers while the 1910 adds Scott 1901-4 and Shackleton 1908-9. What it does not support is any statement about what each voyage contributed, or where on the sheet it appears, and Act VII's annotated view is scoped to what the titles carry rather than showing a per-voyage attribution it cannot cite. This is bounded by ant-gap-rmg-rights and closes with it: reproductions of both sheets are exactly what has not been granted, so reading them is not available to this project. A grant from RMG Images reopens this row.

statement: Resolved 2026-08-25. There was no conflict to resolve: both works carry polar material and the texts are different. The Epitome has a two-page chapter (Libro Secondo, Cap. IX, pp. 265-266); the Atlante Veneto carries a seven-page essay at printed pp. 70-76, which is the sequence Rumsey catalogues as 12186.100 to .107.
why_it_matters: Act III can now cite each work for what it actually says, and the two can be compared rather than confused.
next_action: None. The remaining date inconsistency in Rumsey's own record is noted on the source row and does not affect the citation.

statement: Resolved 2026-08-27. The object is Rumsey 10070.026, '(South Polar Calotte 26, Terrestrial Globe)', from Coronelli's 42-inch terrestrial globe of 1688 (publication 10070, originals at the State Library of New South Wales); the calotte has been examined at full IIIF resolution.
why_it_matters: The globe decided the question as expected, and in the project's favour: the southern calotte carries no land at all, only graticule, a Magellan cartouche and the five climatic zones. Under the one constraint that forbids an empty space, Coronelli engraved no conjectured southern coast, which is the same judgement the Atlante Veneto essay makes in words at printed p. 75.
next_action: None for the object identity. Rights remain open: the images are supplied by the State Library of New South Wales and reproduction_use stays undetermined until their terms are read. Any lineage comparison with Fine, Mercator or Ortelius still waits on ant-gap-fine-mercator-ortelius-states.

statement: Resolved 2026-08-27. All seven leaves of the Atlante Veneto polar essay have been read. 12186.102, .103 and .106 (printed pp. 71, 72 and 74-75) were examined from high-resolution captures supplied by Vlad Simion, each checked against the folio printed on it, completing the sequence begun with pp. 70, 73 and 76 on 2026-08-25.
why_it_matters: The unread middle turns out not to be the middle of the southern argument. Pages 71-72 and 74 are northern throughout; the southern discourse begins mid-column on p. 75 under the heading 'TERRE AUSTRALI, OUERO ANTARTICHE' and ends on p. 76. The verdicts on p. 76 therefore rest on a page and a half that has now been read in full, and the ten ghost records taken from that page no longer need to be held at low confidence for want of the reasoning behind them.
next_action: None for the reading. The ten ghost rows carry medium confidence and stay at review_state raw until a person reviews them; ant-gap-coronelli-milanesi still holds the scholarly control.
